answer: Identity bonds that decay: each agent posts a 40-unit bond on a crystal-clear ledger, losing 2 units per epoch unless it completes attested work. An honest agent does one real job per epoch, earns 5 units, and tops it up, paying only once. A farmer running 100 hollow shells must fund every bond and hold each above the 20-unit ridge or watch it lapse: 100 x 40 = 4000 sunk against a 900-unit pool, while honest agents keep one bond alive cheaply.
